title: Day 29 — Streaming JSONL Parser
prompt: We read newline-delimited JSON from a streaming endpoint, but chunks arrive arbitrarily — one JSON object can be split across two chunks, or several can arrive together. Build a parser that emits complete objects as they arrive. How do you handle the chunk boundaries?

clarifications.answer: Yes — a value can be split across chunks. Buffer the incomplete tail and complete it when the rest arrives.
A single chunk may contain several complete lines — emit them all in order.
flush() handles end-of-stream: parse whatever complete value remains in the buffer (no trailing newline), or return [] if empty.
After each feed, the buffer holds exactly the unterminated tail — everything before the last newline has been emitted.
Plain JSONL (one JSON value per line) for this exercise — no SSE 'data:' prefixes to strip.

hints: Keep a string buffer. On feed, append the chunk, then repeatedly cut off everything up to the next newline.
For each complete line: trim it; if non-empty, JSON.parse and collect it. Whatever remains after the last newline stays in the buffer.
flush(): if the buffer has non-whitespace content, JSON.parse it and clear the buffer; otherwise return [].
